source.note: Adults: 20 mg once daily (ulcer, GERD), 40 mg once daily (gastric ulcer); 20 mg twice daily in H. pylori triple therapy. NOTE: omeprazole only exists as delayed release, which the spec's immediate-release rule does not cover.
Geriatric section: '76% bioavailable ... in healthy elderly volunteers, versus 58% in young volunteers' (single 40 mg buffered solution)
'plasma half-life is 0.5 to 1 hour' model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)

source.citation: Marier JF et al. Pharmacokinetics of omeprazole in healthy adults and in children with gastroesophageal reflux disease. Ther Drug Monit. 2004;26(1):3-8 (PMID 14749542)
source.note: Label gives no Vd. Abstract: apparent V(ss)/F in healthy adults 0.76 +/- 0.26 L/kg. V = 0.76 x 0.58 (model bioavailability) = 0.44 L/kg.
'Peak plasma concentrations ... after repeated doses ... occur within 1.5 to 2 hours' model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)
'The major part of its metabolism is dependent on ... CYP2C19'
'The remaining part is dependent on ... CYP3A4'

source.citation: FDA, 'For Healthcare Professionals | FDA's Examples of Drugs that Interact with CYP Enzymes and Transporter Systems' (content current as of 05/29/2026)
source.note: Table lists omeprazole as '2C19 weak inhibitor'. The label (12.3) calls it 'a time-dependent inhibitor of CYP2C19' without a strength.

'about 77% was eliminated in urine as at least six metabolites'; 'The remainder of the dose was recoverable in feces', implying 'significant biliary excretion' (1 - 0.77 = 0.23). 'little if any unchanged drug' in urine, so no unchanged fraction.

journey.text: Its coating protects it from stomach acid; it is absorbed only after it leaves the stomach, peaking 1.5 to 2 hours later.
Switches off the proton pumps in the stomach lining that make acid.
Quickly broken down in the liver, mostly by the CYP2C19 enzyme; it is gone from the blood within hours.
About three quarters leaves in urine as broken-down pieces; the rest through bile and the gut.
